slides.title: Lesson 6: Thermal Physics Revision — Specific Heat Capacity & Latent Heat
slides.notes: Welcome to Lesson 6: Thermal Physics Revision. Today we bring together Specific Heat Capacity (Lesson 5) and Specific Latent Heat (Lesson 4) so students can confidently distinguish between temperature changes within a single state and state changes at constant temperature.

slides.title: Checkpoint: Spot the Practical Error!
slides.notes: Pair & Share: Why is the experimental SHC higher than the textbook value? Reveal 1: Heat escapes to the surroundings, so ΔE measured > ΔE stored in block (or Δθ is smaller than expected). Reveal 2: Wrap thicker insulation and add a lid.

reveals.question: Why is our calculated SHC higher than the textbook value?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Heat dissipated to the surroundings! Measured energy includes wasted thermal energy.

reveals.question: How can we improve the practical to reduce this error?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Use thicker insulation to minimise heat loss.

slides.title: Solving the Mystery: Specific Latent Heat
slides.notes: Crucial exam distinction: during a change of state, average Kinetic Energy (and therefore temperature) stays constant, while Potential Energy increases as energy weakens or breaks intermolecular bonds.

slides.title: The Great Energy Discrepancy: Why Lv > Lf
slides.notes: Explain why Lv is nearly 7× larger than Lf for water: melting only loosens rigid lattice bonds so particles can slide past one another, whereas boiling completely severs intermolecular attractions and pushes particles far apart against atmospheric pressure.
